chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

"When you have finished supplicating at the grave, go to the pulpit (minbar), wipe it with your hands, and hold its two pommels (rummanatayn), which are the suflawans, then wipe your eyes and face, for it is said that it is a cure for the eye. Stand by it, praise Allah, extol Him, and ask for your need, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'What is between my pulpit and my house is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and my pulpit is on a pasture from the pastures of Paradise.' And the 'tur'ah is the small door. Then go to the station of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and pray in it as long as you wish. When you enter the mosque, send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), and when you leave, do the same, and increase your prayers in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)."

key_terms.التُّرْعَةُ: A small door or passage, specifically referring to the small door connecting the Prophet's house to the mosque.
key_terms.الرُّمَّانَتَانِ: The two pommels or knobs at the top of the pulpit.
key_terms.السُّفْلَوَانِ: The lower parts or bases of the pulpit's pillars.
key_terms.الْمِنْبَرُ: The pulpit or raised platform in the mosque, here referring to the Prophet's pulpit.
key_terms.صَلِّ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ: Send blessings upon the Prophet, a ritual act of invoking divine mercy upon him.
key_terms.مَقَامَ النَّبِيِّ: The station of the Prophet, a specific spot in the mosque where he used to pray.

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended rituals and etiquettes when visiting the Prophet's grave in Medina according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the ritual etiquette (adab) of Ziyarat, specifically highlighting the spiritual significance of the Minbar and the Tur'ah (small door) as extensions of the Prophet's presence. It connects physical acts of reverence, such as wiping the face for healing, with the theological concept of the Prophet's mosque as a 'garden from the gardens of Paradise,' reinforcing the Shia emphasis on intercession and proximity to the Ahl al-Bayt.
